clue.text: Sad paper planes crash in flight

indicators.note: planes that crash end up wrecked, so the letters of these three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy account of model aircraft coming down mid-flight.
explanation.walkthrough: APPLES AND PEARS is Cockney rhyming slang for stairs, so it can stand for a flight of steps. 'Flight' looks like part of the plane story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with stairs, and a flight is a set of stairs.

clue.text: Wonder if mere cello playing makes a nice change

parts.note: wonder is awe, the feeling of amazement

indicators.note: playing music loosely, the letters of these words are performed in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Marvelling at how a cellist's performance livens things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonder' looks like a verb opening a question, but it supplies a noun; 'playing' is the anagram signal on the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings relief from routine is a pleasant break, a welcome respite.

clue.text: Each bit of poetry is sick

parts.note: per means each, as in ten pounds per head
a verse is a stanza, a piece of a poem

explanation.surface: A critic finds every line of a poem distasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick joke or sick mind is twisted and unnatural, the sense of perverse.

clue.text: Complete view of architectural wonder c'est dit!

indicators.note: French for it is said, so the word for the landmark is to be pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: the Eiffel Tower in Paris, the architectural marvel, gives its name

explanation.surface: A Parisian remark on taking in the full sight of a famous landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: The French 'c'est dit' fits the Paris landmark and signals a word said aloud: Eiffel sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a good long look, a full sight of something.

clue.text: See 1 across
Crazy nightmare (short version)

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy or mad
a nightmare experience is hell

explanation.surface: A summary of a bad dream that drives one mad, told briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: '(short version)' looks like a stage direction but is the definition, from the idiom 'in a nutshell'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in a nutshell is to state it briefly, a summary form.

clue.text: I tucked into cake decoration on the outside

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the other word, as food is tucked into

parts.note: to cake something is to plaster it, coat it thickly

explanation.surface: Someone eats a cake that has icing on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' and 'cake' suggest eating, but cake is a verb meaning coat thickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat ornamental column projecting from a wall of a building, an exterior feature.

clue.text: Special song for worker on edge

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A tune written for a labourer living on the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: A national or club anthem is a song reserved for a particular occasion or group.

clue.text: However, the conclusion of Brexit is in more doubt

indicators.note: the pieces before it sit inside the word for more, between its body and its final letter

parts.note: ... are ... helpings, more food
though can mean however, as in he left, though

indicators.note: conclusion means the end, so take the final letter of the word Brexit

explanation.surface: A political commentator says the end of the Brexit saga is ever less certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' is the container signal; 'more' means extra helpings of food, not a comparative. The last letter of Brexit joins the word for however before both go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Second thoughts are reconsiderations, a sense of uncertainty about an earlier decision.

clue.text: Worker and Queen embracing composer of Rule Britannia

indicators.note: one piece hugs the other, holding it inside

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen
Thomas Arne wrote the music for Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A patriotic scene of a labourer, the monarch and the composer of a famous anthem together.
explanation.walkthrough: Rule, Britannia! is a British patriotic song by the 18th-century composer Thomas Arne.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is someone who works for a wage, a breadwinner.

clue.text: Active and extraordinarily tactile with husband

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a lively, touchy-feely spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' rearranges TACTILE together with H.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic person is sporty and physically energetic.

clue.text: Tough to follow Tolkein character — the first solution here?

indicators.note: the word for tough comes after the Tolkien monster in the answer

parts.note: an orc is a goblin creature in Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings
hard means tough

explanation.surface: A fantasy reader finds a Tolkien creature a hard act to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 1 across: apples and pears grow in this place. Tolkien is misspelt 'Tolkein' in the clue as published.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees such as apple and pear are grown together in a planted enclosure of this kind.

clue.text: Gothic country mansion with draughts

definitions.meaning: the Prime Minister's official country house in Buckinghamshire, a grand old pile
the board game, called checkers in the US

explanation.surface: A spooky old country house full of chilly air currents.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence; 'draughts' looks like cold air but is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The PM's country retreat bears this name, and it is also an old name for the board game draughts.

clue.text: Like bird's behind

parts.note: as means like, as in white as snow
a tern is a seabird; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Something resembling the rear end of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird's behind' reads as a bird's rear, but behind is the definition, used of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word for at the rear, towards the back of a vessel.

clue.text: Hankering for times gone by — it's not Poles causing earache

indicators.note: the clue says the longer word is without the two poles, so north and south are removed

parts.note: nostalgia is a longing for the past

explanation.surface: Missing the old days is said to hurt the ears, not the Poles.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles are N and S (north and south); 'it's not Poles' removes both from NOSTALGIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical term for pain in the ear.

clue.text: When drunk, fail to attend church jumble

indicators.note: a drunk slurs his s sounds into sh, so the phrase is said as a tipsy speaker would say it

parts.note: to miss Mass is to skip the church service

explanation.surface: A drunkard skipping the church service ends up in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS MASS slurred by a drunk becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused mixture, a hotchpotch.

clue.text: Blind and quiet state

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
to utter is to state, say aloud

explanation.surface: A sightless, silent condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is a window covering, like a blind that keeps out light.

clue.text: Thus far Auntie, ill and down with no clothing …

indicators.note: each word is stripped of its outer letters, leaving only its middle

explanation.surface: A sick relative, feeling low and undressed so far, trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters from each of Auntie, ill, and, down.
explanation.definitionFit: Until now means up to the present time, so far.

clue.text: … put it on to stay with mother

parts.note: ma is a familiar name for mother
to linger is to stay on, delay leaving

explanation.surface: Continuing from 17, the aunt fakes illness to stay with mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 17's ill aunt. 'put it on' means fake an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to feign sickness to avoid work, to pretend.

clue.text: See 8
Registered winning

definitions.meaning: listed, entered on the official register or list

explanation.definitionFit: Being on the roll means enrolled on a list; being on a roll means having a run of wins.

clue.text: See 15
See 1 down
Beer please. German, right?

parts.note: bitte is the German for please

explanation.surface: A German in a pub politely orders a beer, checking it's the right one.
explanation.walkthrough: German BITTE means please.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a type of British draught ale.

clue.text: Look and smell garden feature

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
BO, body odour, is an unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: Admiring and sniffing a garden's highlights.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a summerhouse or pavilion giving a view over a garden.

clue.text: Flipping bother about 9 or 11 as medicine

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, placed about it
flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to rile is to bother or annoy
the Roman numerals for nine and eleven both work here, IX or XI

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker asks about a remedy for nine or eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' (reversal) also reads as a mild oath; 'about' is the container signal. Nine and eleven in Roman numerals use the same two letters, so either fits.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal potion, a supposed cure-all.

clue.text: In fact, IRA misunderstood final course

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A statement that the IRA was misunderstood after all.
explanation.walkthrough: IRA is the Irish Republican Army, here just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert, served as the last course of a meal.

clue.text: See 5
At the same time halving quaint island item

indicators.note: each of the three words is cut in half, keeping its second half

explanation.surface: A quaint item from an island is cut in two at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the back half of each word: quaINT, islAND, itEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in tandem means doing them together, simultaneously.

clue.text: Lacklustre, nauseating Telegraph, devoid of content or dimension

indicators.note: each word is emptied of its inside letters, keeping only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A critic finds a newspaper dull, sickening and empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is a British daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is one measure of size, alongside width and height.

clue.text: Play more Fats Waller — that's mostly novel

indicators.note: to play is to perform in a fresh way, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for more jazz from Fats Waller, praised as fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Fats Waller was an American jazz pianist. The novel is A Farewell to Arms by Hemingway; without its 'A' the title is 'mostly' there.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's war novel is titled with this phrase plus a leading article, so the answer is most of its title.
